brief.scope: Independent cross-harness review of the GPT-6 docs correction only, against lane-boundary-owner.md. Verify active seeds, imports, onboarding and owning contracts consistently state enduring dev/prod independence: no Symfony app dependency or prod-twin replacement mandate for dev tooling. Preserve the application's Symfony rules and shared wire/provenance. Check precedence, discoverability, historical-record treatment, actual changed links and unsupported claims. Do not count a prompt/doc change as runtime enforcement, demand guard code in this slice, or reopen unrelated defects. Necessary referenced homes only; no whole-lane audit. Return <=1000-word verdict with concrete remaining contradictions, command/ref evidence, coverage and limits. No edits, executable tests, settings/host/DB/network changes or vendor launches. Review the changed documentation, not the planner's separate proposed runtime design.

findings.claim: The withdrawn shared-Symfony/lane-MCP recommendation was banner-corrected in the lever contract but not at the document that carries it. MCP-RESEARCH-2026-09-05.md still reads (line 130) 'That is the candidate for the later Symfony twin, not a reason to introduce a second server during this bounded incumbent-lane change' — a prod-twin replacement frame for lane MCP, uncorrected and undated-as-superseded. It is not a historical class covered by the AGENTS.md blanket clause (it is dated the same day as the correction and is a live scoped recommendation): README.md:344 cites it as the 'research report' behind current lane reads, and ops/conductor/mcp-context-scope.md:3 instructs 'Use MCP-RESEARCH-2026-09-05.md for measured demand'. A reader arriving through either referrer never sees lane-mcp-lever.md's withdrawal.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '118,134p' ops/conductor/MCP-RESEARCH-2026-09-05.md; rg -n 'MCP-RESEARCH' README.md ops/conductor/mcp-context-scope.md; sed -n '4,20p' ops/conductor/lane-mcp-lever.md

findings.claim: A tracked document that active handoff/AAR instructions tell the next session to read first still asserts precedence over the corrected law and still states the retirement doctrine. overview.md:6-8: 'It is not law; the law is AGENTS.md and docs/. Where the two disagree, this document is the newer intent and the law has not yet been updated to match.' overview.md:490-496: the lane is 'in use as-is until each verb's agentscient twin passes the same row, which is the strangler rule ops/README.md already states', and 'It is retired verb by verb'. Two defects: the supremacy clause inverts the precedence AGENTS.md now claims (and is false — the doc is 2026-09-03, the correction 2026-09-05), and the citation to ops/README.md is now dangling, since this change removed that strangler rule (obligation 1 of docs/verified-couplings.md). AGENTS.md's blanket clause names 'handoffs', which arguably reaches it, but the supremacy sentence is read before any blanket and is not itself neutralised.

findings.claim: The added onboarding paragraph says precedence 'comes from AGENTS.md §Lane boundary and precedence and ops/README.md ..., reached through the existing reading list'. The reading list (onboard.py LAW, lines 20-30) is AGENTS.md, CONTRIB.md, instrument-conventions.md, stack.md, coverage-zones.md; ops/README.md is not on it, so it is reached only at a second hop via AGENTS.md §The lane. The lever also correctly disclaims changing the tool's data, but the tool still prints stack.md as 'the stack: layers, incumbents, open seats' — the incumbent frame survives in the served text, and test_onboard_lever.py:52 pins that exact string. No guard code is demanded here; the defect is the doc's overstatement of what the list reaches.

findings.claim: Dangling citations left by the AGENTS.md §The lane rewrite. I-011:14 cites 'twin passes its conformance row (AGENTS.md §The lane)'; §The lane no longer contains a conformance-row/twin rule. ops/docs/README.md:14 still describes the lessons shelf as 'kept so the twins are written better'. envelope.note: Verdict CHANGES. The correction lands its core: enduring dev/prod independence is stated at one owning home (AGENTS.md §Lane boundary and precedence), imported into the cached prefix through CLAUDE.md, and carried into ops/README.md, docs/verified-couplings.md, docs/workflow.md, the conductor and devlane seeds, and the dispatch and task contracts by 17 resolving links. Symfony rules are rescoped to the application rather than removed; shared wire, probes, concerns and provenance are untouched; historical records are banner-superseded, not rewritten; and every changed file disclaims runtime enforcement, which I did not count against it. Two contradictions remain in actively referenced homes. First, the withdrawn shared-Symfony recommendation is corrected only in ops/conductor/lane-mcp-lever.md while its actual home, MCP-RESEARCH-2026-09-05.md, still calls the Symfony MCP bundle 'the candidate for the later Symfony twin' during 'this bounded incumbent-lane change', and is cited as current demand by README.md:344 and ops/conductor/mcp-context-scope.md:3. Second, .dev/wip/overview.md, which active handoff and AAR instructions tell a session to read first, still claims precedence over AGENTS.md and docs/ where they disagree and still states verb-by-verb retirement by twins, citing a strangler rule in ops/README.md that this change removed. Two p3 citation-closure defects follow the same rewrite (I-011:14, ops/docs/README.md:14) and one doc overstatement (onboard-lever.md says precedence is reached through the reading list, but onboard.py's list does not include ops/README.md and still serves stack.md as 'layers, incumbents, open seats'). One unsupported claim rides in the committed record rather than the docs: 20260906T013707Z-code-codex-a46459.json asserts '22 added links/anchors and seed/onboarding references resolve'; I measured 17 boundary-anchor references, all resolving, and could not reconstruct the count of 22 or its basis. No self-approval: this is an independent review by a different harness and model from the producer, with no edits made.
